elements.title: The Empire Brunei (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the opening of The Empire Brunei (pictured) was timed to help create hotel capacity in Brunei for an APEC summit?

elements.title: Herbert Smith (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that museum administrator Herbert Smith hired a special train so that civil servants could watch a total solar eclipse in 1927?

elements.title: Yan Ruisheng (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Yan Ruisheng, China's first full-length feature film, was banned within two years?

elements.title: Shadia Abu Ghazaleh (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Shadia Abu Ghazaleh was one of the first women to join the Palestinian resistance to the Israeli occupation of the West Bank?

elements.title: Radio City Music Hall of the Air (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the radio program Radio City Music Hall of the Air employed approximately 10,000 musicians during the first eight years of its broadcast history?

elements.title: Stanley Washburn (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Stanley Washburn's message on November 29, 1941, warning the US Navy not to underestimate the Japanese, failed to reach Admiral Kimmel before the attack on Pearl Harbor?

elements.title: the first standalone street toilets to cater to both men and women (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the first standalone street toilets to cater to both men and women in Auckland were converted into a male-only facility during the Second World War?

elements.title: Taurus 09 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Taurus 09 was the largest Royal Navy deployment in more than ten years?

elements.title: Kim Jong Un's daughter (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the name of Kim Jong Un's daughter has not been publicly disclosed?
